Reverse every word in a string.problem: Interpret this sheet item as reverse WORD ORDER, retaining letters within words and normalizing whitespace.
Reverse every word in a string.approach: Tokenize whitespace-delimited words, then append them in reverse index order with one separating space.
Reverse every word in a string.pitfalls: The title can also mean reverse letters within each word. This lesson explicitly states its word-order contract; use per-word reversal for the other variant.

Minimum number of bracket reversals to m.problem: For a string of { and }, reverse individual braces to make it balanced; return minimum reversals or -1.
Minimum number of bracket reversals to m.approach: Cancel matched pairs. Remaining unmatched braces consist of closes then opens. Two closes or two opens need one reversal; odd leftover counts each need rounding up.
Minimum number of bracket reversals to m.pitfalls: An odd total length can never balance. Parenthesis-type mixing requires a different contract.

Count and say.problem: Starting at term 1="1", each next term describes runs of the previous term.
Count and say.approach: For every maximal run, append its length then its character. Runs partition the old term, producing one unambiguous next term.
Count and say.complexity: O(sum of generated term lengths) time; O(max consecutive term lengths) memory.
Count and say.pitfalls: n is one-based. Read a completed previous string; do not mutate it while discovering runs.

Hashing In Strings | Theory.theory: Polynomial hash represents a sequence by a modular weighted sum. Prefix hashes plus powers permit O(1) substring-hash calculation after O(n) preprocessing. Equal hashes do NOT prove equal strings: collisions exist. Double hashing reduces accidental collisions but does not make equality exact. For exact matching verify candidate characters or use KMP/Z. Java long multiplication may overflow before modulo; choose a modulus/base whose intermediate product fits, or use an overflow-safe multiply. Normalize subtraction modulo a positive modulus. A rolling hash removes the outgoing high-order digit, multiplies by base, and adds the incoming digit.

Rabin Karp Algorithm.problem: Find all exact pattern matches, using rolling hashes as a filter and direct verification for collisions.
Rabin Karp Algorithm.approach: Compute the initial polynomial hash, then remove the outgoing character's contribution, shift by base, and add the incoming character. Matching hashes trigger exact regionMatches.
Rabin Karp Algorithm.complexity: O(n+m+candidateCount*m) time; O(1) auxiliary space plus output. Worst case O(n*m), including repetitive true matches.
Rabin Karp Algorithm.trace: aba hash matches window 0 and window 2; both are verified before emitting.
Rabin Karp Algorithm.pitfalls: Hash equality alone is not exact matching. Products fit long for this chosen base/modulus and UTF-16 alphabet.

Z function.problem: z[i] is the longest prefix matching the suffix beginning at i; z[0]=0 by convention.
Z function.approach: Maintain the rightmost prefix-matching box [l,r]. Inside it, reuse the corresponding earlier Z value capped at the box boundary, then extend comparisons beyond that boundary.
Z function.complexity: O(n) time; O(n) returned array, O(1) extra state.
Z function.trace: aaaaa: from position 1 match four letters, then reuse progressively shorter box matches.
Z function.pitfalls: Index 0 has differing conventions; here it is explicitly zero. Use a separator absent from the alphabet for pattern+separator+text matching.

KMP Algorithm or LPS array.problem: Return all zero-based starts of pattern in text, including overlapping matches. Empty pattern matches every boundary.
KMP Algorithm or LPS array.approach: LPS stores each prefix's longest proper prefix that is also suffix. On mismatch, fall back to that border rather than rechecking known characters. After a match, fall back to allow overlaps.
KMP Algorithm or LPS array.complexity: O(n+m) time; O(m) failure array plus output.
KMP Algorithm or LPS array.trace: ababa contains aba at 0; after matching, keep border a and match again at 2.
KMP Algorithm or LPS array.pitfalls: Do not reset pattern index to zero after every full match; that loses the efficiency/border invariant.
KMP Algorithm or LPS array.alternatives: Direct comparison at each start is O(n*m) worst time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Shortest Palindrome.problem: Add characters only at the FRONT to make a shortest palindrome. Input is ASCII/ordinary BMP characters, excluding surrogate-pair semantics.
Shortest Palindrome.approach: Find the longest palindromic prefix via LPS on s, a unique sentinel, and reverse(s). The unmatched suffix must be mirrored in front; no shorter addition could cover it.
Shortest Palindrome.trace: Longest palindromic prefix is aacecaa; unmatched a is mirrored in front.
Shortest Palindrome.pitfalls: A literal separator might appear in input; integer sentinel -1 cannot equal a char value. StringBuilder.reverse handles surrogate pairs differently from the code-unit LPS, so the stated character contract matters.

Longest happy prefix.problem: Return the longest NONEMPTY proper prefix that is also suffix, or empty if none.
Longest happy prefix.approach: The final LPS entry is exactly the largest proper border length for the entire string.
Longest happy prefix.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) failure-array space plus output.
Longest happy prefix.trace: level begins and ends with l, but no longer proper prefix matches its suffix.
Longest happy prefix.pitfalls: The full string is not a proper prefix. Empty input has no nonempty border.
